title: SLA, RTO and RPO: what the company promises and what it can deliver

videos.script: A contract says the service will be available 99.9% of the time. It sounds like a guarantee. It is not. It is a price, paid in credits, when the service falls short. {{price}} This lesson is about the numbers a company promises, and whether the network behind them can keep the promise. {{numbers}} First, three terms that people mix up. What you measure, what you aim for, and what you sign. {{three}} Then the error budget. The minutes a month the service is allowed to be down, and what may spend them. A failover of three seconds barely touches it. One restore by hand can spend it all. {{budget}} Then two numbers for the day things go wrong. How long until the service is back, and how much data you can afford to lose. {{timeline}} You will see why a promise cannot be stronger than the chain it rests on. {{chain}} And last, what backups and replication really give you, and why a replica copies your mistakes as faithfully as your data. {{backup}}
